meta.note: The ticker spine: the join between the dependency graph and anything with a price. Station lists are copied from stations.json and validated against it on every build, so this file cannot drift away from the corpus.
meta.attribution: A company at nine stations must not be counted nine times. Every entry carries weights that sum to one. The default basis is `even` — an equal split, which involves no judgement and is fully reproducible. Where an even split would be visibly absurd (NVIDIA appears at nineteen stations) the weights are hand-set, marked `judgement`, and carry a one-line reason. None of them are segment disclosures, and the view offers the even split alongside so you can see how much the judgement moved the answer.

kinds.label: Listed
kinds.note: Has a primary listing. Contributes to market-cap aggregates once quotes are ingested.

kinds.label: Division
kinds.note: Part of a listed parent. Attributing a parent's whole market cap to a division is wrong and attributing zero is also wrong, so each carries an estimated `parentShare` — an estimate, flagged as one.

kinds.label: Private
kinds.note: No listing. Counted in exposure and never in market-cap aggregates. A private mark and a public price are never silently mixed.

kinds.label: Institution
kinds.note: Research institute, consortium, standards body or state agency. No market value at all, and no attempt is made to invent one.

kinds.label: Not an organisation
kinds.note: The demand-side entries in stratum 27 — enterprises, developers, consumers. They exist in the corpus as endpoints, not as companies.

meta.cik: Left null on purpose. CIKs are resolved from the SEC's own ticker-to-CIK map at ingest time rather than typed by hand, because a hand-typed CIK is a silent wrong answer.
meta.caveat: This is a partial spine by design. PLAN.md's guidance was to start with the names carrying most of the stack's value rather than all 533, so aggregates computed from it are lower bounds on a layer and must be labelled as such. Coverage per stratum is computed and shown.
